paperMetadata.title: Rethinking Model Interpretability and Mechanistic Understanding Design

abstract: In recent years, the interpretability of transformer models has become a critical research area, given their widespread adoption in natural language processing tasks. This paper introduces a novel framework for enhancing model interpretability and mechanistic understanding by integrating attention analysis with causal intervention techniques. We propose a new architecture modification that allows for fine-grained control over attention mechanisms, facilitating deeper insights into the model's decision-making processes. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach not only improves interpretability but also maintains competitive performance on benchmark datasets. The primary contributions of this work include a novel attention modification technique, a systematic evaluation of interpretability metrics, and a comparative analysis against state-of-the-art methods. We also discuss the implications of our findings for future research in model interpretability.

contributions.title: Attention Mechanism Modification
contributions.description: We introduce a new modification to the attention mechanism that allows for more granular control and interpretability by dynamically adjusting attention weights based on external intervention signals.
contributions.novelty: This technique provides a new way to dissect and understand attention behaviors in transformers, offering insights not available through traditional static analysis.

contributions.title: Comprehensive Interpretability Evaluation
contributions.description: We develop a systematic framework for evaluating model interpretability using a set of proposed metrics that measure both global and local interpretability.
contributions.novelty: Unlike prior works, our evaluation framework provides a balanced assessment across different levels of interpretability, facilitating more informed comparisons between models.

contributions.title: Comparative Analysis with SOTA
contributions.description: We perform a detailed comparative analysis with state-of-the-art interpretability methods, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of our approach.
contributions.novelty: This analysis is the first to comprehensively position a new method within the existing landscape of transformer interpretability techniques.

methodology.problemFormulation: The challenge is to enhance the interpretability of transformer models without sacrificing performance, by understanding and modifying their internal mechanisms.
methodology.approach: We propose a modification to the attention mechanism involving external signals that influence attention distributions. This is achieved through a novel architecture that incorporates causal interventions.

components.name: Dynamic Attention Controller
components.role: Modifies attention weights based on external intervention signals.
components.details: Implemented as an additional layer that processes intervention signals and adjusts attention scores using a learned transformation.

components.name: Causal Intervention Module
components.role: Intervenes in the attention process to identify causal relationships.
components.details: Uses a set of pre-defined intervention signals to perturb attention distributions and analyze resultant outputs.

assumptions: Intervention signals are representative of meaningful external factors.
The modified attention mechanism does not degrade model performance beyond acceptable thresholds.
limitations: The approach requires pre-defined intervention signals, which may limit applicability across diverse domains.
Increased computational complexity due to additional layers and intervention processing.

evidence.description: Validation of interpretability enhancement through attention modification.

setup.context: Evaluating modified transformers on standard NLP tasks.

evaluation.protocol: Models are compared across tasks with and without intervention, measuring interpretability and task performance.

results.notes: Lower entropy indicates more focused attention distributions.

evidence.analysis: The modified model exhibits enhanced interpretability with focused attention distributions, while maintaining performance comparable to the baseline.

evidence.description: Application of the method to a sentiment analysis task.

setup.context: Sentiment prediction on a balanced dataset.

evaluation.protocol: Assessing model explanations with and without intervention through human evaluation.

results.notes: Scores reflect improved clarity and relevance of explanations with intervention.

evidence.analysis: Interventions enhance the model's ability to provide meaningful explanations for sentiment predictions.

works.summary: Introduced the transformer architecture and highlighted the role of self-attention in capturing dependencies.
Analyzed the interpretability of attention weights in transformers, questioning their reliability as explanations.
Developed probing techniques to analyze linguistic knowledge in BERT's internal representations.
Explored causal interventions in transformer attention to understand their decision-making processes.
Investigated emergent language understanding capabilities in large language models.

futureWork.direction: Development of automated intervention signal generation
futureWork.motivation: To facilitate broader applicability of the method by reducing the need for manually defined intervention signals.

futureWork.direction: Exploration of interpretability in multimodal models
futureWork.motivation: To extend the applicability of interpretability techniques to models that process multiple types of data, such as text and images.
